body.x: ChinaByte, a Chinese IT and ICT outlet, named YHDATABASE, ORGO Co., Ltd. and NRT Sensors its top three innovative companies at the FIX 2026 Global Media Awards.

The Future Innovation tech eXpo 2026 (FIX 2026) ran from Oct. 21 to Oct. 24 at EXCO in Daegu, featuring future mobility, robotics, and AI and ICT technologies and products. In the Global Media Awards, overseas outlets review technologies and products on the show floor, and each outlet chooses its own top three companies.

ChinaByte (比特网) is a Chinese technology outlet founded in 1997 that covers enterprise ICT, AI, robotics, semiconductors, smart mobility and other industrial technology. Its main readers are corporate executives and technology and business decision-makers in China, and it focuses on analyzing the industrial value of technologies and how companies stand in the supply chain. It joined FIX as a global media partner in 2026 after FIX 2024, and Stephanie Chen, its editor-in-chief, covered the show and took part in the awards selection.

The three companies ChinaByte picked cover different technology areas: AI-based data analysis software, drive and lifting components for logistics robots, and precision position-measuring sensors. The selection reflects that the strength of intelligent industrial systems depends not only on AI software but on the core components and sensors that enable a robot's actual movement and precise control.
YHDATABASE Applies AI and Big Data to Financial Risk Analysis and Security

YHDATABASE provides AI- and big data-based abnormal financial transaction detection, financial risk management and mobile security solutions, drawing on its experience in financial security and public-sector informatization. Its flagship solution, y-SmartData, analyzes electronic financial transaction data to detect abnormal transactions and supports financial institutions' risk management work such as anti-money laundering (AML) and internal control.

In addition to analyzing each user's transaction patterns, y-SmartData uses graph-based analysis to examine connections among accounts, transactions and users, and is designed to find signs of fraud that individual transactions would not reveal. The company also offers other solutions, including y-SmartChat, a generative AI-based AI agent tailored to public institutions, companies and organizations, as well as malicious app detection and mobile device monitoring.

As AI spreads across industries, data analysis, security and risk detection are becoming base technologies behind digital transformation. YHDATABASE is notable because it can extend the data analysis and anomaly detection technology it built in the financial sector to risk management needs in other industries. It is less a case of embodied intelligence or robot hardware than an example of AI software that supports the operation and reliability of intelligent industrial systems.
ORGO LIFT Gives Logistics Robots Their Lifting Motion

ORGO Co., Ltd. is a robot component company that develops and supplies electric lifts mounted on AGVs and autonomous mobile robots (AMRs). Its flagship product, ORGO LIFT, is the core component that gives logistics robots their lifting function, supporting the raising and lowering of materials and goods.

ORGO LIFT has position control and synchronization control functions and is designed to connect with robot systems through CAN communication, RS232 communication and PLC control. These functions matter because they let logistics robots do more than carry goods: they can also handle loading and unloading.

As logistics automation expands, AGVs and AMRs are used to move materials and automate tasks in factories and distribution centers. In that setting, a robot needs not only mobility but also the mechanical and control capability to lift cargo precisely and carry out operations at set positions. ORGO's electric lift is a component that makes a logistics robot's actual work functions possible, which is why it draws attention as technology supporting embodied intelligence and the industrial automation ecosystem.
NRT Sensors Raises Robot Control Precision With Interference-Resistant Encoders

NRT Sensors develops and manufactures position measurement and sensor technology, including magnetic, optical and inductive encoders, resolvers and potentiometers. An encoder is a component that measures the position and angle of a motor or rotating shaft and sends it to the control system, helping robots and automation equipment carry out target motions precisely.

Based on its range of encoder technologies, the company develops products for collaborative robots, service robots, factory automation equipment and motor control. Its inductive encoders in particular are designed to support precise position measurement while reducing the effects of the external environment, such as magnetic interference, dust and vibration. They offer absolute position measurement of 20 bits for single-turn and 24 bits for multi-turn, and a measuring speed of up to 6,000 RPM.

For a robot to perceive its surroundings and perform complex tasks, it needs not only AI models and sensors but also technology that accurately measures and controls the positions of joints and motors. An encoder's precision and environmental resistance affect a robot's repeatability and stable operation. By developing encoders for different environments and equipment and strengthening domestic manufacturing capacity, NRT Sensors ties into the core component supply chain for robotics and motion control.
AI, Core Components and Precision Control Behind Embodied Intelligence

In its FIX 2026 pre-event interview, ChinaByte pointed to the rise of embodied intelligence, which connects digital intelligence with the physical world. It named core components such as robot hands and servo joints, the integration of AI and hardware, and the potential for on-site demonstration in logistics and industry as its main interests. As criteria for the Global Media Awards, it stressed a technology's potential for commercialization, mass-production capability, cost competitiveness, supply chain value and potential for Korea-China industrial cooperation.

ChinaByte's top three span different technology fields: AI-based financial risk analysis software, electric lifts for logistics robots and high-precision encoders. YHDATABASE supports the reliability and operating efficiency of digital work through data analysis and risk detection, ORGO provides mechanical and control components that give logistics robots their lifting motion, and NRT Sensors provides sensor technology for precise position measurement in robots and automation equipment.

As industrial competition moves beyond technology demonstrations toward stable mass production, cost competitiveness and supply chain cooperation, companies with expertise in core components and software can play an important role in international markets. The selection is expected to highlight these companies' industrial uses and their potential to join global supply chains, and to give Korean and Chinese companies a chance to explore technology cooperation and business ties.

Ten overseas media outlets from Europe, the Americas and Asia took part in the FIX 2026 Global Media Awards, including ChinaByte. Each outlet reviewed the technologies and products of exhibiting companies and chose its own top three. Selected companies gain an opportunity to be publicized through overseas media.

The press corps included Leo Thevenet, editor-in-chief of Le Café du Geek, an IT, lifestyle and global technology outlet; Juan Castromil, editor-in-chief of Clipset, a Spanish mobile and consumer electronics outlet; Eliane Fiolet, editor-in-chief of Ubergizmo, a Silicon Valley outlet covering IT and consumer electronics innovation; Davis Kim, reporter at AVING USA, a global technology, business and exhibition outlet; Yoshioka Tomomi, editor-in-chief of Otaku Soken, a Japanese outlet covering subculture and AI, virtual reality and IT convergence technology; Sherri Wang, research editor at DIGITIMES, a global outlet covering semiconductor and ICT supply chains; Võ Hoàng Long, reporter and deputy editor-in-chief of VietnamPlus, a Vietnamese state-run general news portal; Stephanie Chen, editor-in-chief of ChinaByte, a Chinese outlet covering IT, enterprise digital transformation (DX) and AI; Dimpal Bajwa, deputy editor of ET Manufacturing, an Indian outlet covering smart factories, robotics and manufacturing technology; and Mubashar Aftab, founder and publisher of Pokde.Net, a Malaysian outlet covering IT hardware, gaming and mobile technology.

The media partners took part in the FIX 2026 Innovation Awards Media Day and in on-site judging for the BEST OF FIX 2026 Global Media Awards during the show, and covered firsthand news from innovative companies set to lead Korea's future industries, introducing it to readers around the world.
